newsitem.title: USA: Unicom unit forms district cooling venture.
newsitem.headline: Unicom unit forms district cooling venture.

text.p: Unicom Thermal Technologies Inc, a Unicom Corp subsidiary, said Wednesday it formed its third district cooling joint venture.

In its latest partnership, Unicom Thermal joined HL&P Energy Services, a subsidiary of Houston Industries Inc, to develop a cooling network for Houston's central business district as well as other cities in the southwest.
Last year, Unicom Thermal joined with Boston Edison Co and Ontario Hydro to bring district cooling technology to Boston, Mass. and Windsor, Ontario, Canada.

The newest company, operating under the name Northwind Houston LP, will manufacture large-scale blocks of ice at night. During the day, the ice is melted and pumped through a distribution network to buildings for use in air-conditioning.
After circulating through customer buildings, the warmed water returns to the district cooling sites for re-chilling.
Construction for the Houston cooling system is expected to begin during the second quarter of 1997 with service starting in 1998.
